book.title: The International System of Garment Cutting, including Coats, Trousers, Breeches, and Vests, with Diagrams and Full Instructions for Dealing with all Forms of Disproportion
book.author: J. P. Thornton
book.publisher: The Thornton Institute, 24-25 Castle Street East, Oxford Street, London W. (published by J. P. Thornton)
book.year: undated; after 1910 (the book reports the 1910 lecture that introduced the 'new International Coat System', p. 5); probably c. 1911-1912
book.scan_source: Library of the Swedish National Armoury (Livrustkammaren), photographed 2019, uploaded to archive.org
book.archive_metadata_warning: archive.org gives the date as 1885; that is wrong (the book reports events of 1910)
book.units: inches; all girth measures are HALF measures (half breast 18 = a 36 breast)
book.scale: the 'scale' is a working number in real inches, two-thirds of the width shoulder measure (27 x 2/3 = 18); divisions such as '1/6 scale' are fractions of that number in real inches; no graduated tape is involved
book.drafting_position: p. 22: 'All patterns should be drafted in the position shown on the diagram page.' On Plate 16: A top left; line A-B runs down (centre-back construction line, toward the hem); line A-C runs to the right (top line, toward the front); front at the right.
book.seams: no separate seam allowance is added anywhere in the lounge text; shoulder measures are taken over the coat; ease and seams are inside the '+' quantities (e.g. waist measure plus 2 1/2); p. 378 says the usual allowance taken up in making is 'two quarter-inch seams'. Seams therefore appear to be INCLUDED in the drafted lines (inference, flagged). Inlays: no amounts given for the lounge.
book.notation: dist(P,Q) = straight distance between drafted points; len(...) = length measured along a drafted curve; measure names as in 'measures'. Formulas are a literal reading of the printed rule; where reading the rule needed tailoring convention the note says so.
book.fraction_style: printed mixed numbers (superscript fractions) are written here as 16½ etc.; printed slash fractions are kept as 1/2 etc.

measures.name: natural_waist_length
measures.description: First measure, A to B fig. 1 (Plate 1): from the seventh vertebra (top of back closing seam) to a point on the back seam level with the side hollow of the waist; taken over the coat (pp. 17-18). Lounge text: 'Waist Length'.

measures.name: fashion_length
measures.description: Length of the coat from the top of the back seam (lounge text: 'Skirt length, 29 inches'; rule B: 'fashion length, 29 inches'). Third measure A to D fig. 1 is the skirt length for body coats.

measures.name: across_back
measures.description: Fourth measure, back width (or stretch), E to F fig. 2; 'decided by fashion' (p. 17). Listed in the lounge measures line (7½); the sleeve draft uses the back width measured on the draft, X to N (7¼).

measures.name: elbow_length
measures.description: Fifth measure, E to G fig. 2 (continued from across back to elbow).

measures.name: sleeve_length
measures.description: Sixth measure, E through G to H fig. 2 (continued to hand); 'a quarter of an inch below the outer bone of the wrist is generally correct'.

measures.name: width_shoulder
measures.description: Seventh measure, A, B, C, to D fig. 3: from a point on the back closing seam level with the centre of the scye, over the hollow of the front shoulder, down and around the front of the scye, under the arm and back to the start; taken closely over the coat.

measures.name: depth_shoulder
measures.description: Eighth measure, E, B, C, F, to E fig. 3: from a mark on the coat collar one inch below the desired crease edge of the collar at the centre back, over the front shoulder hollow, around the front of the scye and diagonally up back to the mark; normally 1 inch more than width_shoulder.

measures.name: half_breast
measures.description: Ninth measure, I to J and around chest fig. 4, coat open, over the waistcoat, truly horizontal; used as a half measure ('Breast, 18', 'the breast measure (18)').

measures.name: half_waist
measures.description: Tenth measure, K to L and around on vest fig. 4, in the hollow of the waist; used as a half measure ('Waist, 16'). Rules saying 'waist' mean this half measure.

measures.name: half_seat
measures.description: Eleventh measure, M to N and around fig. 5, over the trousers; used as a half measure ('Seat, 19'). Rules saying 'seat' mean this half measure.

measures.name: scale
measures.description: Derived working divisor: 'Two-thirds of width shoulder (27) gives the scale (18).' Header prints 'Width shoulder measure, 27 ⅔ = 18 inch scale'. For the normal model (p. 22) all divisions are taken from the half breast instead.

measures.name: shoulder_excess
measures.description: Derived: depth_shoulder minus width_shoulder ('Depth shoulder measure, 28 = 1 inch excess'). Rule I uses half of it.

pieces.name: framework (lines shared by back and forepart)

steps.rule_verbatim: Instructions. Draw lines A B and A C.
steps.direction: A-B straight down from A (centre-back construction line); A-C square to it, to the right (top line)
steps.note: Plate 16 shows A as the top-left corner of a rectangle; the front (C, Z, J) lies along the right.

steps.rule_verbatim: D from A, 1/2 inch,
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Top of the back closing seam (nape).

steps.rule_verbatim: E from D waist length, 16½ inches.
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Waist level. The waist line squared across from E (E, F, Q, QQ, TT, P, S, SS on Plate 16) is not ordered in the text; the diagram shows it.

steps.rule_verbatim: B from D, fashion length, 29 inches.
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Bottom level. The bottom line squared across from B (to BB) is not ordered in the text; the diagram shows it.

steps.rule_verbatim: 2—E, 9 inches.
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Hip level. The hip line squared across from 2 (2, 3, 6, 4, 5 on Plate 16) is shown only on the diagram.

steps.rule_verbatim: H from A, 1/2 scale measure (9).
steps.direction: down line A-B

steps.rule_verbatim: I from H, half difference between “width” and “depth” measures (1/2 inch).
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Scye-depth (breast) level.

steps.rule_verbatim: In the absence of shoulder measures make I from H a 1/2 inch.
steps.direction: down line A-B
steps.note: Alternative to F07.

steps.rule_verbatim: Square line I towards J.
steps.direction: square across from A-B, to the right
steps.note: Breast line: carries O, M, T, R, V, Z, J, JJ on Plate 16.

steps.rule_verbatim: F from E, 1¼ inches.
steps.direction: square in from A-B along the waist line (to the right)
steps.note: Printed '1 ¹/₄'. Hollow of the back seam at the waist.

steps.rule_verbatim: O from I, and 3—2, half of F—E.
steps.direction: along line I-J, to the right
steps.note: One printed step fixes two points (O and 3). No value printed; French column gives 'O—I, et 3—2, 1 ½ cm'.

steps.rule_verbatim: O from I, and 3—2, half of F—E.
steps.direction: along the hip line from 2, to the right
steps.note: Second point of the same printed step.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve line D to OF, and 3.
steps.direction: curve D - O - F - 3
steps.note: Printed 'D to OF'. Diagram: below 3 the seam runs straight down, parallel to A-B, to the bottom line at B's level.

steps.rule_verbatim: G from A, 1/6 scale less 1/2 inch (2½).
steps.direction: along line A-C, to the right
steps.note: Printed '1 6 scale' with the slash lost in the scan (OCR '1 6'); French/German '1/6'.

steps.rule_verbatim: K from I, 1/3 scale (6).
steps.direction: up line A-B (diagram: K lies between D and H)
steps.note: Direction not stated in text; Plate 16 places K above I on A-B.

steps.rule_verbatim: L from K, 1/3 scale plus 1½ inches (7½).
steps.direction: square across from A-B at K, to the right (diagram)
steps.note: Back shoulder point.

steps.rule_verbatim: M is squared down from L.
steps.direction: straight down from L to line I-J
steps.note: M = foot of the perpendicular from L on the breast line.

steps.rule_verbatim: GG to G, 1/8 inch.
steps.direction: down from G (diagram)
steps.note: Back neck point. The back neck curve D-GG is not ordered in the text; the diagram shows a shallow curve from D rising to GG.

steps.rule_verbatim: Draw shoulder seam GG to L.
steps.direction: straight GG to L
steps.note: Plate 16 draws wavy marks along the outer part of this seam (fulling, see p. 53).

steps.rule_verbatim: L to N, 2 inches.
steps.direction: down line L-M
steps.note: Plate 16 marks N with a notch on the back scye; N is the hind-arm sleeve pitch used by the sleeve draft.

steps.rule_verbatim: W from M, 1/12 scale (1½).
steps.direction: diagram only: diagonally up and forward from M (about 45 degrees, into the angle between L-M and the breast line)

steps.rule_verbatim: LL to L, 1/2 inch.
steps.direction: diagram: beyond L, continuing the shoulder seam GG-L outward
steps.note: Point of the back shoulder.

steps.rule_verbatim: Q from F, 1/3 waist (5⅓).
steps.direction: along the waist line, to the right
steps.note: DUPLICATE: the English column gives Q twice. This first pair (B14, B15) has no counterpart in the French or German columns (French has 'On courbe la couture de côté' here). The diagram measures F-Q at about 5.9 in, nearer the second rule (B17).

steps.rule_verbatim: 4 from 3, as Q to F, plus 1 inch.
steps.direction: along the hip line, to the right
steps.note: DUPLICATE of B18 (see B14).

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve LL, N, and W.
steps.direction: curve LL - N - W
steps.note: Diagram: the curve continues below W to the side seam just above M; wavy marks along it (worked in, p. 53).

steps.rule_verbatim: Q from F, 1/3 waist, plus 1/4 inch (5⅝).
steps.direction: along the waist line, to the right
steps.note: Matches French 'Q jusqu'à F 1/3 ceinture, plus 1 cm' and German. Printed value damaged '(5 ⁵ ₈)', read 5⅝.

steps.rule_verbatim: 4 from 3, 1/3 seat measure, plus 1/4 inch (6⅝).
steps.direction: along the hip line, to the right
steps.note: Matches French '4 jusqu'à 3, 1/3 bassin, plus 1 cm'.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve line M, Q, and 4 to bottom.
steps.direction: curve M - Q - 4, continued to the bottom line
steps.note: Diagram: straight below 4 to the bottom line; balance marks '=' near M.

pieces.name: forepart (front, with lapel, buttons and pocket)

steps.rule_verbatim: R from O, 2/3 scale. (12).
steps.direction: along line I-J, to the right
steps.note: OCR CORRECTION: the R is damaged in print and reads as 'K'/'κ'; French 'R jusqu'à O 2/3', German 'R von O, 2/3 skala (32)', and the next line 'S is squared down from R' confirm R.

steps.rule_verbatim: S is squared down from R.
steps.direction: straight down from R to the waist line
steps.note: Plate 16 continues this vertical below the waist to pocket point 7.

steps.rule_verbatim: T from R is 1/2 inch.
steps.direction: along line I-J toward the back (to the left; diagram)
steps.note: Bottom of the front scye.

steps.rule_verbatim: U from T, 1/12 scale (1½).
steps.direction: straight up from T (diagram)

steps.rule_verbatim: V from T, 1/6 scale (3).
steps.direction: along line I-J, to the right

steps.rule_verbatim: C is squared up from V.
steps.direction: straight up from V
steps.note: Front neck point. The text does not say how far up; Plate 16 places C on the top line A-C produced (level with A).

steps.rule_verbatim: Draw front shoulder seam, C—L.
steps.direction: straight line C to L (the back shoulder point)
steps.note: Construction line; Plate 16 draws it dot-dash.

steps.rule_verbatim: X from C, 1/4 inch less than back shoulder seam.
steps.direction: along line C-L
steps.note: Front shoulder point. Plate 16 writes '½' at the end of the front shoulder: the drawn front shoulder seam ends at a point about 1/2 inch below X, and curves from C to it (diagram only; hatching along it = strain out, p. 53).

steps.rule_verbatim: Y from U, one half of T—U (3/4).
steps.direction: square forward from U, to the right (diagram)

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve scye and shoulder seams.
steps.direction: diagram: front scye from the front shoulder end through Y and T, round the bottom and back toward the side seam near M
steps.note: Shape fixed by the diagram only. A notch on the front scye about 0.6 in forward of T and 0.4 in above the breast line (measured on the scan) is the forearm pitch (RR of Plate 46).

steps.rule_verbatim: Z from O, the breast measure (18).
steps.direction: along line I-J, to the right

steps.rule_verbatim: C to NN, 1/6 scale.
steps.direction: down the line C-V (diagram)
steps.note: LABEL REUSE: Plate 16 shows two points named NN, one on C-V at this depth and one on the vertical through Z at the same level, joined by a dashed line. The neck curve (P13) passes through the second one; XX (P15) is measured from it.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve neck C through NN.
steps.direction: curve from C down and forward through NN (the NN on the Z vertical)
steps.note: Diagram: the gorge line continues straight past NN and XX to the top of the lapel.

steps.rule_verbatim: SS from S half waist plus 1/4 inch (8¼).
steps.direction: along the waist line, to the right
steps.note: Centre front at the waist.

steps.rule_verbatim: J from Z, 2¼ inches ;
steps.direction: along line I-J, to the right
steps.note: Centre front at the breast line.

steps.rule_verbatim: NN to XX, 1 inch.
steps.from_point: NN (second NN, on the vertical through Z)
steps.direction: forward (to the right) at NN's level
steps.note: Top of the front (centre-front) line.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve front line XX, J, SS, 5 and BB.
steps.direction: curve XX - J - SS - 5 - BB
steps.note: Centre-front (buttoning) line. Points 5 and BB are not given rules: diagram shows 5 where the hip line meets this line and BB where the bottom line meets it.

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure F to Q. Place this amount at SS and measure out to TT, the waist measure plus 2½ inches (18½).
steps.direction: back along the waist line, to the left
steps.note: Tailoring idiom 'place this amount at SS and measure out to TT': the tape reading dist(F,Q) is put at SS and TT is where the tape reads waist + 2½; the formula is that reading (interpretation, flagged). 18½ is the printed total, not the distance SS-TT.

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure TT to Q, and take out from Q to QQ, one third of such amount (   ).
steps.direction: along the waist line, toward TT (to the right)
steps.note: The book prints EMPTY brackets here: no worked value is given. QQ is the forepart side seam at the waist.

steps.rule_verbatim: The remaining two-thirds (   ) is divided equally from point P at under arm “fish.”
steps.direction: along the waist line either side of P
steps.note: Empty brackets in print. POINT P HAS NO RULE IN THE TEXT. Diagram: P is on the waist line about 1.0 in behind (left of) T's vertical, about 3.3 in forward of M's vertical (measured on the scan, ±0.3 in). The fish (shaded) starts on the bottom of the scye about 1.4 in behind T and ends about 4.3 in below the waist at the pocket mouth.

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure seat, 3 to 4. Place this amount at 5, and measure out to point 6, the real measure, plus 3 inches (22).
steps.direction: back along the hip line, to the left
steps.note: Same idiom as P18 (interpretation, flagged). 22 is the printed total. Diagram: 6 falls behind (left of) 4, so the forepart overlaps the back below the waist.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve side seam as diagram.
steps.direction: diagram: from the scye near M through QQ and 6 to the bottom
steps.note: Shape fixed by the diagram only.

steps.rule_verbatim: SSS from BB, 1/12 waist.
steps.direction: down from BB (front line produced below the bottom line)

steps.rule_verbatim: JJ from J, 1 inch.
steps.direction: forward (to the right) along line I-J
steps.note: Front edge at the breast line = break point of the lapel (the crease line starts here on Plate 16).

steps.rule_verbatim: 12 from SS, 1¼ inches.
steps.direction: forward (to the right) along the waist line
steps.note: Front edge at the waist.

steps.rule_verbatim: SS is 1/12 waist measure below line.
steps.direction: below the bottom line
steps.note: Last line of the English column; first letter clipped in print/scan, reads 'SS'. French 'SSS sont 1/12 de ceinture en bas de la ligne', German 'SSS ist 1/12 ...': read SSS, a repeat of P23.

steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: No rule. Diagram: front edge from JJ down through 12, roughly parallel to the front line to about the hip line, then rounding away to meet the bottom about 5½ in behind SSS (measured). Bottom of the forepart slopes down from the side seams to the SSS level.

steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: No rule for lapel width, lapel point or step. Diagram: on the flat pattern the edge rises from JJ to a lapel point on the gorge line produced, about 1.1 in forward of XX; the crease (roll) line is drawn from JJ up past the neck, passing about 0.8 in in front of C at C's level (cf. collar rule C from CC 3/4 in, p. 124). The lapel and collar end are also drawn turned back over the crease line, showing the notch (step) and dashed stitching; no dimensions are written. Wavy marks along the crease = bridle (p. 53).

steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: No rule. Diagram: four buttonhole marks on the front line, the first at the breast line (J) and the others about 4 in apart below it (one just below the waist line, last about 12 in below the breast line); each a short bar running from the front line toward the edge.

steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: No rule for point 7 or the pocket. Diagram: 7 is on the line squared down from S about 4½ in below the waist line; a flap pocket about 7 in wide and 2 in deep hangs from a mouth through 7, its back end meeting the bottom of the fish. No breast pocket drawn.

steps.rule_verbatim: C from CC, 3/4 in. always.
steps.direction: diagram: beyond CC on the forepart shoulder line produced past the neck point
steps.note: LABEL REUSE: on the collar diagram CC is the forepart neck point (the lounge's C) and C is the new point. Direction is not stated; Plate 49 Dia. 2 shows C just beyond CC, on the crease line.

steps.rule_verbatim: Draw crease row A to B.
steps.direction: straight line from A through C, produced to B
steps.note: A is the break point on the front edge (lounge: JJ, by diagram; no rule here). Plate 49 draws A-G-C-B as one dashed line.

steps.rule_verbatim: B from C, same as A—B on back.
steps.direction: along the crease row produced beyond C
steps.note: 'A—B on back' = the back neck on Dia. 1 (A centre back, B back neck point); on the lounge back that is the curve D to GG (label reuse).

steps.rule_verbatim: D from B, 1/2 in.
steps.direction: diagram: square to the crease row at B, toward the shoulder side

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve crease row D, C, G.
steps.direction: curve D - C - G
steps.note: G has no rule: diagram shows G where the lapel crease row crosses the gorge.

steps.rule_verbatim: E from D, the stand, 1¼ in.
steps.direction: diagram: on the line B-D produced beyond D
steps.note: Collar stand at the centre back.

steps.rule_verbatim: F from D, the full measure (1 8/8).
steps.direction: diagram: on the line D-B produced beyond B (opposite side from E)
steps.note: AMBIGUOUS PRINT: the value reads '1 ⁸/₈' (numerator unclear). Most likely 1⅜ (the dress-coat collars on the same page print 'F from B, 1 ³/₈'); French/German give 3¾ cm (about 1½ in); on the diagram F-D is drawn noticeably longer than E-D. 'Full measure' = stand plus fall at the centre back.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve outline as diagram.
steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: Sewing-on edge from E to the gorge, fall edge from F to the collar point, and the collar end/step: diagram only, no dimensions written.

steps.direction: Plate 46 Dia. 1
steps.note: The sleeve takes measurements from the body draft (Dia. 1): X on the back closing seam level with N; N hind-arm pitch on the back scye (lounge: L to N 2 in, p. 54); NN just below N (another draft, p. 48: 'NN from N, 1/2 in.'); RR forearm pitch notch on the front scye (no rule; diagram shows it where a line from the corner of the small square at the front scye meets the scye). LABEL REUSE: lounge X is the front shoulder point, not this X.

steps.rule_verbatim: B from A, a straight line.
steps.direction: straight line from A (diagram: horizontal, to the left)

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure back from X to N (7¼).
steps.direction: measured on the body draft
steps.note: Printed '(7 ¹/₄)'; the measures line says across back 7½.

steps.rule_verbatim: Place this amount at A, and continue to C, 2/3 of scale, less 1 in. (11).
steps.direction: along line A-B
steps.note: Idiom: the tape reading dist(X,N) is placed at A and C is marked where it reads 2/3 scale less 1 (11). Formula is that reading (interpretation, flagged); 11 is the printed tape reading.

steps.rule_verbatim: Continue to elbow (F) 20½,
steps.direction: along line A-B
steps.note: Same tape continued; 20½ is the printed tape reading.

steps.rule_verbatim: and hand (B) 31.
steps.direction: along line A-B
steps.note: 31 is the printed tape reading.

steps.rule_verbatim: By F cast the curve B to BB.
steps.direction: arc from B centred on F

steps.rule_verbatim: D from C, 1/2 scale, less 1/2 in. (8½).
steps.direction: square up from line A-B at C (diagram)

steps.rule_verbatim: Square down to point G.
steps.direction: from D, square to C-D, toward the hand end (parallel to A-B)
steps.note: How far along this line G lies is not stated; the diagram puts G at the hand end above BB.

steps.rule_verbatim: BB from G is 1/3 scale, or to taste.
steps.direction: cuff line from G to the arc of S06
steps.note: Cuff width; 'or to taste'.

steps.rule_verbatim: Square F, BB, and G.
steps.direction: not explained
steps.note: Wording unclear; diagram shows the line squared up from F to H, and the cuff line G-BB.

steps.rule_verbatim: H is squared out from F,
steps.direction: square up from A-B at F to the line D-G

steps.rule_verbatim: I from H, 1 in.
steps.direction: along line D-G toward D (diagram)

steps.rule_verbatim: J from I, 1 in. Curve forearm.
steps.direction: down from I into the sleeve (diagram)
steps.note: Hollow of the forearm at the elbow.

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure scye (Dia. 1), from hind-arm (N) to forearm (RR), say 9½ i
steps.direction: measured along the scye of the body draft
steps.note: Printed 'say 9 ¹/₂ i' ('in.' cut short in print). 'say' = an example value.

steps.rule_verbatim: Make sleeve from A to K, same amount (9½).
steps.direction: diagram: K lies on line C-D produced just beyond D
steps.note: Text does not say K is on C-D produced; the diagram shows it.

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve forearm from K, through J to G.
steps.direction: curve K - J - G

steps.rule_verbatim: E is midway between C and D.
steps.direction: on C-D

steps.rule_verbatim: L from E, one half of A—K, plus 1/2 in. (5¼).
steps.direction: square out from C-D at E, away from the sleeve (diagram)

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve sleeve head and hind-arm.
steps.direction: diagram: head K - L - A; hind-arm from A dipping slightly below line A-B toward F and up to BB
steps.note: Shapes fixed by the diagram only.

steps.rule_verbatim: Under side. Measure scye (Dia. 1) NN to RR (7½).
steps.direction: measured along the scye of the body draft
steps.note: NN and RR have no rule in the lounge text (see S00).

steps.rule_verbatim: Measure sleeve, K to M, 1/2 in. more (8).
steps.direction: diagram: along the under-sleeve top curve from K to M, M lying near A on the hind-arm side

steps.rule_verbatim: Curve under side as diagram.
steps.direction: diagram only
steps.note: Below M the under sleeve shares the top sleeve's lower parts (forearm, elbow, cuff) on Dia. 2.

construction_order_note: Order of the printed English lines on p. 54 ('2—E' and 'F from E' share the printed line of 'B from D'; 'O from I, and 3—2' is one printed step split here into B02 and B03; 'Curve neck C through NN' is printed before 'C to NN'). Diagram-only items (P27-P30) and the collar and sleeve follow their own pages.
